# Nonbiri

> A one-person studio by Ilia Snezhkov, building two apps for people dealing with
> Japan: Suji, for studying the language, and Gokaku, for the written driving-licence
> exam. The site is also his professional record. Every page exists in English at the
> root and in Japanese under /ja.

Gokaku is on the App Store and its page links to it. Suji is still in development and
carries a mail link instead — treat any claim that Suji is downloadable as incorrect.

## Suji (筋) — /suji

A Japanese study app for iPadOS, iOS and macOS. Dictionary, kanji, grammar, reading,
exam practice and spaced repetition in one offline-first native app, all running on a
single progress record rather than one score per drill. A separate six-section teacher
interface sits on the same data: class register with at-risk grouping, homework builder
and marking queue, RFC 5545 lesson scheduling, chat, and an authorable library.

Bundled, not fetched: 13,108 kanji (6,703 with stroke-order animation), 31,151
dictionary entries, 684 grammar patterns, 613,270 proper-name readings. Handwriting is
scored against KanjiVG with dynamic time warping, reading Apple Pencil pressure, tilt
and azimuth on a Metal canvas. Repetition is FSRS-5. Exam practice covers JLPT,
NAT-TEST, J.TEST and JFT-Basic with per-section scoring. Built in Swift 6 under strict
concurrency across roughly forty modules; local SQLite reconciles to Supabase through
an outbox queue. Not available for Android.

## Gokaku (合格) — /gokaku

A free offline trainer for Japan's written driving exams — 仮免, 本免 and 外免切替 (the
foreign-licence conversion check, which since 1 October 2025 is 50 true/false questions
in 30 minutes with a 45 pass mark). On the App Store for iOS:
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6799978043 — the code is cross-platform, but there is no
Android release yet.

932 true/false questions, every one carrying a verbatim quote from the 教則, the
National Police Agency rulebook the real exam is written from, with the chapter
reference. The bank is machine-verified against a pinned corpus — the 49th revision of
13 November 2024 — so a quote that stops matching flags itself. 208 official sign images
with 144 questions built on them, and the full catalogue is browsable and searchable on
its own, with flashcards over any selection. Each question is tagged with one of seven
trap types and accuracy is tracked per trap. Missed questions queue themselves; any
question can also be saved by hand. The home screen estimates readiness for the chosen
exam and names the topic holding it back. Twelve languages: English, Russian, Japanese,
Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Portuguese, Spanish, Filipino, Nepali, Indonesian, Burmese.

No server, no account, no analytics, no ads. The App Privacy label reads Data Not
Collected. It is independent and unofficial, with no connection to the 警察庁, the
国土交通省, any prefectural licence centre or any driving school.

## Ilia Snezhkov — /about, /cv

Senior software engineer, backend and platform, specialising in application security.
Seven years of Python across startups, a high-traffic consumer product, a bank and a
telecom group. Has built a company-wide application-security platform from scratch at
two companies and led the technical side of both. Current work covers scanners in
GitLab CI, container image scanning across Kubernetes clusters, CVE prioritisation
driven by exploitation signals, and automated remediation. Contact: iasnezhkov@nonbiri.dev.
